8bZh5LMaSmE.title: RailsConf 2014 - All the Little Things by Sandi Metz
8bZh5LMaSmE.summary: Sandi Metz takes an ugly section of conditional code and refactors it into a few simple objects, bridging object-oriented theory and practice. The talk includes her take on the Gilded Rose refactoring kata and the idea that duplication is cheaper than the wrong abstraction.
8bZh5LMaSmE.why: HN treats it as a top-tier programming talk for learning refactoring and for the wrong-abstraction principle, recommended repeatedly over a decade.

quote.text: this talk captures all the important values in a single example.

ON0A1dsQOV0.title: Gtk to Qt - a strange journey [linux.conf.au 2014]
ON0A1dsQOV0.summary: Dirk Hohndel explains why the Subsurface dive log project migrated from Gtk to Qt, the obstacles encountered, and advice for other applications frustrated with Gtk. It is a linux.conf.au 2014 talk.
ON0A1dsQOV0.why: Go-to reference in GTK versus Qt debates, valued for a candid account from experienced developers who tried both toolkits.

quote.text: One of the best discussions on the subject, made by old hackers, but new guys to GUI programming, who tried both

hEUO6pjwFOo.title: Intelligence and Stupidity: The Orthogonality Thesis
hEUO6pjwFOo.summary: Robert Miles explains the orthogonality thesis: how an agent can be highly intelligent while pursuing goals that seem stupid or alien to humans. He separates intelligence from goals and touches on the stamp-collector example.
hEUO6pjwFOo.why: HN people use it as the standard short explanation for why AI can understand human ethics without sharing them, and often recommend the whole channel.

quote.text: this video to me states the problem in a nutshell (that whole channel is gold)

zrpUDuUtxPM.title: Floyd Toole - Sound reproduction – art and science/opinions and facts
zrpUDuUtxPM.summary: Floyd Toole's CIRMMT distinguished lecture on the science of sound reproduction, drawing on decades of blind listening research. It covers what listeners prefer in loudspeakers and why measured accuracy and anechoic response matter.
zrpUDuUtxPM.why: HN recommends it as a crash course on audio reproduction science, especially the finding that listeners reliably prefer more accurate speakers in blind tests.

quote.text: In blind testing, the average listener reliably prefers the more accurate speaker.

kUfF2MTnqAw.title: Why You Should Put YOUR MASK On First (My Brain Without Oxygen) - Smarter Every Day 157
kUfF2MTnqAw.summary: Destin Sandlin of Smarter Every Day undergoes hypoxia training and experiences his own impaired thinking as oxygen is withdrawn. The video shows how quickly and unnoticeably oxygen deprivation degrades judgment, illustrating why you put your own mask on first.
kUfF2MTnqAw.why: It is the go-to demonstration of how hypoxia silently disables decision making, cited in threads on altitude, flying, diving, CO2 and breathwork.

quote.text: has a wonderful video demonstrating this effect [0]. I’d recommend watching the whole thing

bx3KuE7UjGA.title: MINIX 3: a Modular, Self-Healing POSIX-compatible Operating System
bx3KuE7UjGA.summary: Andrew Tanenbaum's FOSDEM 2010 talk on MINIX 3, a microkernel OS built for high reliability and security. It shows how the system detects and recovers from device driver crashes, and addresses microkernel performance concerns.
bx3KuE7UjGA.why: HN points to it as an accessible explanation of microkernel isolation and fault-tolerant design, and as Tanenbaum's answer to performance objections.

quote.text: it's a very interesting but accessible talk for those interested in lower-level systems and fault-tolerant architectures.

1H3xQaf7BFI.title: THE NVIDIA AI GPU BLACK MARKET | Investigating Smuggling, Corruption, & Governments
1H3xQaf7BFI.summary: A Gamers Nexus investigative documentary on the black market for Nvidia AI GPUs, following smugglers, middlemen, and buyers, including reporting from China. It examines how export-restricted chips reach their users.
1H3xQaf7BFI.why: HN recommends it as real on-the-ground reporting on how banned GPUs get into China despite export controls.

quote.text: Gamers Nexus has a good video where his team travelled to China and did some actual investigative journalism

xKu2de0yCJI.title: AT&T Archives: Saul Bass Pitch Video for Bell System Logo Redesign
xKu2de0yCJI.summary: The 1969 pitch film in which Saul Bass presents the Bell System logo redesign to AT&T, part of the largest corporate re-identity program in U.S. history.
xKu2de0yCJI.why: HN holds it up as a masterclass in explaining and selling a design.

quote.text: I always go back to the Saul Bass presentation to AT&T over their 1970 logo redesign.

-i6wvix6buI.title: High Volume, Bandwidth Heavy Infrastructure On The Cheap - Kyle Drake
-i6wvix6buI.summary: Kyle Drake of Neocities explains the bandwidth pricing pitfalls of the big cloud providers. He describes how to run high-volume, bandwidth-heavy infrastructure far more cheaply, including through co-location.
-i6wvix6buI.why: HN recommends it whenever cloud egress costs come up, since it gives concrete numbers on real bandwidth costs versus cloud pricing.

quote.text: Check out this talk by Kyle Drake that goes more into the details of bandwidth costs

BD6h-wDj7bw.title: Why Women Are Stripey
BD6h-wDj7bw.summary: Veritasium explains X-chromosome inactivation, where different cells in a woman's body switch off different X chromosomes, giving a mosaic pattern. It uses animation from the WEHI institute and connects to calico cat coloring.
BD6h-wDj7bw.why: Commenters point to it as the best short explanation of X inactivation and why calico cats and some human traits are mosaics.

quote.text: Veritasium has a fantastic video that discusses the genetics behind the random color patterns of calico cats

Wp7GAKLSGnI.title: Oral History of Donald Knuth Part 1
Wp7GAKLSGnI.summary: A roughly three-hour Computer History Museum oral history interview of Donald Knuth by Edward Feigenbaum, recorded in 2007. Knuth covers his family, music, early programming, his thesis, The Art of Computer Programming, and the detour into TeX and METAFONT.
Wp7GAKLSGnI.why: HN recommends it as a superb, personal long-form look at Knuth's life and work habits.

quote.text: It's a _really_ long interview, +7 hours. But it's also superb.

EL7Au1tzNxE.title: Vibe coding complex changes in Rust
EL7Au1tzNxE.summary: Jon Gjengset spends about three hours livecoding complex changes in a Rust codebase with agentic AI tools, testing his hypothesis that AI is weak at non-pattern work. He documents where Claude Code helps and where it struggles.
EL7Au1tzNxE.why: Pointed to as a non-promotional, realistic long session of an experienced engineer working with AI on non-trivial code.

categories.name: C, C++, Rust, Go & systems languages

quote.text: I found this one and sat down and watched the whole three hours.

I6IQ_FOCE6I.title: Here Comes Another Bubble v1.1 - The Richter Scales
I6IQ_FOCE6I.summary: A cappella parody song by The Richter Scales, set to Billy Joel's 'We Didn't Start the Fire', lampooning the Web 2.0 startup bubble. It won a Webby for viral video in 2007.
I6IQ_FOCE6I.why: Resurfaces in threads on startups, valuations and hype cycles as a funny, prescient bubble satire.

quote.text: in case anyone missed this gem.

aT7mnSstKGs.title: DEFCON 19: Bit-squatting: DNS Hijacking Without Exploitation (w speaker)
aT7mnSstKGs.summary: Artem Dinaburg's DEF CON 19 talk on bit-squatting, where flipped bits in DRAM cause devices to contact domains that differ by one bit from legitimate ones. He shows how registering such domains can hijack traffic without exploiting any software bug.
aT7mnSstKGs.why: HN cites it in ECC memory debates and bit-flip discussions as concrete evidence that memory errors have real security consequences.

quote.text: There was a good Defcon talk about some security implications of this phenomenon

v2Q_zHG3vqg.title: Multithreading the Entire Destiny Engine
v2Q_zHG3vqg.summary: A 2015 GDC talk by Bungie's Barry Genova on how Destiny's engine was restructured into a job graph with limited thread pre-emption. It is aimed at programmers of demanding game engines.
v2Q_zHG3vqg.why: HN points to it as a real-world example of game engine multithreading and of safety annotations in C.

quote.text: explaining how Bungie turned almost every part of Destiny's engine into a job graph that can be processed in parallel

-2ml6sjk_8c.title: Tesla crashes into concrete barrier....ON AUTO PILOT!
-2ml6sjk_8c.summary: A short amateur clip of a Tesla Model S on Autopilot failing to follow a lane shift in a construction zone and hitting a concrete barrier. The uploader uses it to argue against driverless trucks.
-2ml6sjk_8c.why: Cited as a concrete example of Autopilot's limits whenever threads debate self-driving safety and Tesla's claims.

quote.text: Here's a good example - a Tesla on autopilot crashing into a temporary road barrier which required a lane change.

SiB8GVMNJkE.title: Fight Club - The Recall Coordinator's Formula
SiB8GVMNJkE.summary: A two-minute clip from the film Fight Club in which the narrator, a former recall coordinator, explains the formula companies use to decide whether a recall costs more than paying out settlements.
SiB8GVMNJkE.why: Cited whenever a thread shows a company weighing cost against safety or customer harm.

quote.text: I'm reminded of the delightful opening scene of "Fight Club" where the narrator explains that his job is to apply "The Formula".

lj3iNxZ8Dww.title: Miss Teen USA 2007 - South Carolina answers a question
lj3iNxZ8Dww.summary: A one-minute clip of Miss Teen USA 2007 contestant Miss South Carolina giving a rambling, incoherent answer to a pageant question. It became a widely shared internet meme.
lj3iNxZ8Dww.why: Only posted as a joke reaction to someone's muddled or incoherent argument, not as something to watch for content.

mQT5aMa_7iI.title: Gabbard Diagram for Low Earth Orbit 1959-2021
mQT5aMa_7iI.summary: An animated Gabbard diagram of objects in low Earth orbit from 1959 to 2021, showing altitude over time. It highlights major debris-generating events and how low-altitude debris decays out of orbit.
mQT5aMa_7iI.why: HN uses it to illustrate orbital debris evolution and how altitude determines how fast debris decays.

quote.text: See this video for evolution of debris and altitude over time

sJO0n6kvPRU.title: [HD] Children of Men - Ark of the Arts - "I just don't think about it"
sJO0n6kvPRU.summary: A scene from Children of Men in which Theo visits Nigel in the Ark of the Arts to get transit papers. It features Nigel's line "I just don't think about it" and a one-handed chorded keyboard.
sJO0n6kvPRU.why: HN cites it as a film example of chorded input devices and as an analogy for wealthy indifference to suffering.

quote.text: I imagine something like this clip from Children of Men could work
